subject: POC success criteria & next steps — Atlas Payments trial
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC success criteria & next steps — Atlas Payments trial

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed plan so we’re aligned before we spin up the trial environment.

Call summary (5 min):
- Goal: validate Redwood inference for real-time fraud-detection assist in the Atlas payment flow.
- Primary constraint: 99th-percentile latency and total inference cost; secondary: model quality / false positive rate.

Proposed POC (2-week sandbox):
1) Success criteria (what Atlas will measure):
   - Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end inference latency < 200 ms (avg expected ~120–150 ms)
   - Throughput: sustain 50 inference requests/sec with <= 250 ms p95 under steady-state load
   - Cost: inference cost <= $0.0005 per token (target) or overall per-request cost budget of $0.02
   - Quality: human-review false positive rate <= 2% on flagged transactions; intent-match / model decision alignment >= 95% on labeled set

2) Evaluation plan:
   - Week 1: integration + smoke tests using 1k historical events (anonymized) + correctness eval on labeled dataset (n=500)
   - Week 2: performance soak test (ramp to 50 req/s), cost reporting, and final joint review

3) Ownership & roles:
   - Atlas: Alex — provide anonymized sample payloads, labeled set, and primary POC contact
   - Redwood: Jordan — commercial lead; Marissa — CS lead for onboarding and quality eval; Ben — solutions engineer for infra, perf tuning, and test harness

4) Deliverables:
   - POC plan doc (attached)
   - Day 3 checkpoint + perf report at end of Week 2
   - Draft SOW for signature if we hit success criteria

Next steps:
- Alex to confirm sample payload delivery timeline (do you have 48–72 hours to share a small labeled sample?)
- We’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff early next week (Mon/Tue) to get engineering aligned

I attached a one-page POC plan and a draft SOW for context.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0199

Attachments: POC-plan-v1.pdf, SOW-draft.docx

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@atlas-payments.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & next steps — Atlas Payments trial

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear recap. This looks good and aligns with what the execs want to see. A few clarifications from our side:

- Latency: the 200 ms p95 target is acceptable, but we also track 99th pct; if p99 goes above 350 ms we’ll need a fallback path for the payment decision (we can tolerate a short window where we fall back to the current rule engine).
- Throughput: 50 req/s is a reasonable steady-state target. We’ll also test burst traffic up to 150 req/s for short spikes.
- Cost: the per-token guidance helps — we’ll track per-transaction economics.
- Quality: labeled set of ~600 transactions (mix of fraud/non-fraud) available; I’ll anonymize and share via S3 link by end of day Wed.

We can do kickoff Tue 29th at 10am PT. Ben, can you confirm if Redwood needs any network configs or IP allowlists?

Alex Chen
Senior Engineering Manager — Fraud Ops
Atlas Payments
alex.chen@atlas-payments.com

On Mon, Sep 28, 2026 at 08:22 AM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Great — thanks Alex.
>
> I’ll send a calendar invite for Tue 10am PT and Ben will share an infra checklist ahead of the kickoff.
>
> —Jordan

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@atlas-payments.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 07:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & next steps — Atlas Payments trial

Alex/Jordan —

Quick infra/ops checklist for kickoff and what I’ll deliver during the POC:

- Network: we’ll provide a hostname and IPs for allowlisting; no inbound VPC peering required for the sandbox (we’ll call your endpoint), but if Atlas prefers private connectivity we can discuss Dedicated options later
- Data: sample payload schema needed + anonymized S3 link (we’ll pull from there)
- Test harness: I’ll set up a load test harness (k6) to ramp to 50 req/s steady and spike to 150 req/s for 60s to validate p95/p99.
- Metrics we’ll collect: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/request, cost/token estimate, requests/sec, error rate, and model confidence distribution
- Quality eval: will run labeled set (n=600) and produce a confusion matrix + precision/recall/FPR. We’ll also provide a small human-review batch of ~100 flagged transactions for manual validation (Marissa will coordinate)
- Timeline: Kickoff Tue (29th) -> Integration & smoke tests by Day 3 -> Week 1 labeled-set quality eval -> Week 2 perf soak + final joint review on Fri 9/10 (end of Week 2)

I’ll attach the perf checklist to the kickoff invite. If Alex can confirm S3 link ETA (Wed EOD) and any IP allowlist windows, I’ll start provisioning.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: infra-checklist.md

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: POC success criteria & next steps — Atlas Payments trial

Alex —

Perfect — thanks for the quick turnaround. Calendar invite sent for Tue 10am PT with Ben/Marissa on the call.

Action items before kickoff:
- Alex: share anonymized S3 link for labeled set (ETA Wed EOD) — Alex confirmed in thread
- Ben: post infra checklist on the invite and provide IPs for allowlist (Ben to do)
- Marissa: prepare human-review instructions and the 100-sample batch workflow
- Jordan: finalize POC plan (attached) and circulate SOW draft after Week 2 if success criteria met

We’ll treat the acceptance criteria as the source of truth for whether we move to SOW. If anything changes on Atlas side re: timeline or evaluation targets call it out on the kickoff.

Thanks all — excited to get started.

Jordan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
